Answer: D
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined, peripheral parenchymal consolidation in the left lower lobe with visible air bronchograms, which is a classic radiological presentation of Bronchiolitis Obliterans Organizing Pneumonia (BOOP/COP). This finding aligns with the clinical history of persistent infiltrates unresponsive to antibiotic therapy, distinguishing it from typical bacterial pneumonia or malignancy.
